source.title: Tunneling the Loss Landscape: Bypassing Memorization with Monte Carlo Parameter Swapping
source.authors: Lai-Shun Chan; Xiaotian Zhang; Yue Shang; Ge Zhang; Entao Yang

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. It refers to a technical supplement, but that supplement is not included.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures delayed train/test generalization on a small modular-arithmetic task using training and test accuracy, the central measurement in the original grokking claim, though with a different arithmetic task and added interventions.
record.gate_note: Rows record reported grokking-time or relative test-accuracy outcomes. The study does not vary training-set size. PM, RC, and FD findings are not rows for these claim versions because they do not measure the circuit formation or circuit-specific progress measures named in V2. Referenced results from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study trains a 1-layer transformer on (x^2+y) mod 67 and reports train and test accuracy. Under AdamW, test accuracy reaches 99% about 3000 epochs after training accuracy reaches 99%. That baseline observation bears directly on V1. Most of the paper, however, uses grokking as a testbed for glass-dynamics diagnostics and its own SAM-Swap method. Only the baseline and comparator settings bear on the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that grokking's memorization phase is glass-like kinetic arrest in parameter space, shown by collapsed mobility, aging and channel-like trajectories. They also conclude that perturbations (SAM-Swap, weight decay, large noise) accelerate generalization by promoting diffusion-like exploration. They frame this as direct dynamical support for the glass-relaxation interpretation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a 1-layer transformer on (x2 + y) mod 67, with a 30% test split and 20-run averages, and adds glass-dynamics measurements and perturbation interventions; the paper says it follows a prior glass-theory setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Generalization timing changes with the training intervention: the paper reports earlier generalization for AdamW with a weak probe, Adam with large Gaussian noise, and SAM-Swap than for Adam with a weak probe. SAM-Swap swap ratio also affects stability and timing: r = 10−2 is reported as most stable and fastest, while smaller ratios recover baseline grokking and larger ratios induce excessive fluctuations.

fits_no_version.finding: During the memorization phase, parameter mobility collapses (dR falls from ~1 to ~1e-2, then toward 1e-4). Replica correlation plateaus and shows aging with waiting time. Trajectory fractal dimension collapses to about 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The memorization plateau of grokking shows glass-like kinetic arrest: low mobility, history dependence and channel-like trajectories.

fits_no_version.finding: Randomly swapping parameter values within a layer, triggered when FD falls below 1.1, cuts grokking time to ~650 epochs, compared with ~3000 for AdamW.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Structured perturbations that restore exploration in parameter space shorten the grokking delay.

record.problems: Training-set size is not varied. The paper reports averages over 20 runs but gives no uncertainty estimates for the grokking-time values in the text. The authors note that FD estimates depend on a fixed 20-epoch window and are sensitive to sampling choices; this limits the mechanism evidence but does not alter the accuracy outcomes recorded here.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows were omitted. PM, RC, and FD results were not included because they do not measure the versions tested here.

untested.parts: Training-set size is never varied (fixed 70/30 split), so the claim that the delay grows as the training set shrinks is untested.

missing.what: Epoch at which training accuracy reaches 99% in the baseline. Needed to quantify the memorization-to-generalization gap; the text only says memorization begins at ~1e2 epochs.
Grokking times for Adam+probe, AdamW+probe and Adam+Noise, shown only graphically.
Swap-ratio sweep, which the text says recovers baseline grokking at smaller ratios; details are in a supplement not included.

record.verdict_notes: The tranche is borderline between T1 and T4, since much of the paper is about the authors' own diagnostics and method. T1 is kept because the baseline grokking delay is reported under a close recipe. V7 is not tested: the study perturbs training but does not control adaptive-optimizer instability or softmax precision, and the delay persists under all settings. Hyperparameters were chosen to minimize grokking time. Results are averaged over 20 runs, but no uncertainty is reported for any value.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not vary training-set size, so it does not test whether smaller training sets require more optimization.

It measures parameter mobility, replica correlation, and trajectory fractal dimension, but does not track formation of a generalizing circuit, removal of memorizing components, or circuit-specific progress measures.
No non-algorithmic data are tested, and initialization scale or weight norm is not systematically varied to switch grokking on or off.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is tested.
The study does not test whether low norm favors a more efficient generalizing circuit, nor does it test a critical dataset size or ungrokking below one.
The study does not identify or compare algorithms learned across runs.
The study does not control or test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point limits in the softmax as explanations for the delay.

relationships.condition: Unperturbed or weakly probed training (AdamW lr 1e-2, wd 1e-1; Adam with sigma=1e-5 probe) on (x^2+y) mod 67
relationships.reason: Test accuracy reaches 99% about 3000 epochs after training accuracy reaches 99% under AdamW (r1). Adam+probe and AdamW+probe also show delayed generalization (r2, r3).
relationships.display_finding: Under AdamW, test accuracy reached 99% about 3,000 epochs after training accuracy reached 99%, with delayed generalization also occurring under probed Adam and AdamW.

relationships.condition: Adam with large additive Gaussian parameter noise (sigma=1e-2)
relationships.reason: Noise injection shortens the delay relative to Adam+probe (r4). The delay's length therefore depends on optimization perturbations, not only on the task.
relationships.display_finding: Adding Gaussian parameter noise with σ=1e-2 shortened the delay relative to Adam+probe.
